newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Nov 5.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Nov 5.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Melbourne Cup fever hits the nation today with today's running of the prestigious A$2.2 million race. Of the 24-horse start-up, favourites include Oscar Schindler (5-1), Saintly (6-1), Nothin' Leica Dane (7-1), Doriemus (8-1), Senator (10-1), Arctic Scent(15-1) and Istidaad (16-1). Page 24.

The Canterbury-Bankstown Rugby league club is considering applying for the second National Basketball League license on offer in Sydney. The NBL will receive bids for the license at its annual general meeting early next year. Page 20.

The Australian Cricket Board Chairman's XI slumped in the early stages yesterday in reply to the West Indies 9-256 from 50 overs, before a massive 96 not out from Brendan Julian in just 52 balls ensured victory with eight overs to spare. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Lloyd Williams, chairman of Melbourne's Crown Casino, has led the gambling action in today's Melbourne Cup run, backing topweight Doriemus to win more than A$1 million today. Without the increased pressure imposed by Williams, the Bart Cummings-trained Doriemus, at 7-1, will attempt to be the fourth horse to win back-to-back Melbourne Cups. Page 40.

After a stint in Adelaide, Davis Cup tennis will return to Sydney for the first time in almost seven years with Tennis Australia deciding to stage the event at White City, Paddington, from February next year. The first Davis Cup clash will see Australia met France on the grass court. Page 39.

Australian Wallaby coach Greg Smith has hinted at a number of changes for the make-up of the front row that helped defeat Italy 40-18 last month, with New South Wales captain and prop Andrew Blades tipped to make his rugby union Test debut against Scotland at Murrayfield on Saturday. Page 39.
THE AGE

Irish jockey Michael Kinane has arrived in Melbourne a day late from Hong Kong to ride Oscar Schindler in the Melbourne Cup at Flemington today. Oscar Schindler has eased from 7-2 to 5-1 as firm favourite for the great race. Page C12.

Victory in the Melbourne Cup has been elusive for veteran jockey Darren Gauci. With today's ride on Few Are Chosen (50-1) being his 11th Melbourne Cup, Gauci hopes to change his fortunes. After weighing in at 50.5 kilograms today he rates Few are Chosen as a genuine cup chance. Page C12.

Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor says the wheels have not fallen off his team, despite failing to win a match in India. Taylor claims his team is now focusing on the series against the West Indies that is to begin in less than three weeks. Page C11.
HERALD SUN

Michael Kinane, rider of Melbourne Cup favourite, Oscar Schindler, paid a visit to the Flemington track yesterday, declaring the 3,200-metre course "perfect". Kinane said there would be no excuses for the boom import not to perform today. The Irish gallopr's odds firmed to 5-1 yesterday. Page 76.

The West Indies did not hesitate to reveal their fresh talent to Australia, playing them on the cricket Tour opener in Perth yesterday. Most of the interest in the ACB President's XI match revolved around West Indies fast bowlers Patterson Thompson and Nion McLean. Page 70.

1996 Australian Football League Grand Final winners North Melbourne will continue to fiercely push the AFL to play its opening round home-and-away match on Good Friday of next year. North Melbourne, specialists at the Friday night opener, would also like some proceeds of the match to go to the Good Friday appeal held by the Royal Children's Hospital. Page 70.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Ex-Australian Football League full-forward Darren Bennett called on his past to make a spectacular touchdown-saving tackle in the San Diego Chargers' victory over the Indianapolis Colts, 26 to 19, in yesterday's NFL clash. Page 66.

After six winless weeks, the Australian Cricket team today leaves India with plans to reverse current fortune with a successful Test series against the West Indies, starting in Brisbane on November 22. Captain Mark Taylor is confident his squad can turn around following the bizarre events of the one-day series on the "plasticine" pitches of India. Page 60.

According to respected English ratings organisation Timeform, the fears held by every Australian owner and trainer with a runner in today's Melbourne Cup that giant Oscar Schindler may be too good and too well weighted for the great race are justified, with the ratings group claiming that only bad luck will stop the Irish galloper from winning. Page 65.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
